newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer urges quick action on German tax reform.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer urges quick action on German tax reform.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday urged the German parliament's arbitration committee to find an early agreement between the major parties on terms of a tax reform to allow this to go ahead.
In a bracketed aside to the printed text of his speech at a reception in the Bavarian town of Aschau, Tietmeyer said:
"We must hope that at least the arbitration committee will come quickly to convincing actions, for example on the tax reform."

Tietmeyer referred to a comment from President Roman Herzog that Germans tended to have relatively little problem in assessing problems, but considerably more of a problem in putting the solution into place.
But he added, "The future capability of the German consensus model will be proven by the ability to turn these assessments into action."

The German consensus model -- under which government, industry and unions work closely together -- has come under attack in recent years as pressures within the system grow in the face of increased international competition.

Tietmeyer made clear in his speech, a text of which was released in Frankfurt in advance of delivery, that reform was essential throughout the German economy to help reduce unemployment and increase competitiveness.

"However important a stable monetary environment may be for a healthy economic development, the euro will not magically resolve problems in the jobs market or in the area of public finances," Tietmeyer said, referring to the single currency due for launch in 1999.
He called for "courage and determination" in carrying out necessary domestic reform.
In addition to the overhaul of taxes currently under discussion, Germany is working to reform its pensions and liberalise its rigid labour markets.
